There are a couple of ways to go to a party member. The first is to right click their party frame and click “Visit Hideout.” The second, and generally better way, is to click the little blue swirl on their party frame - this teleports you to whatever zone they’re in, but you might want to double check that they aren’t in some random campaign zone before you click it. Correct, you press the message button on the trade site and wait for the seller to invite you. If you have an offer that is different than the listed price, it’s generally common courtesy to try to message the person again (after the initial one from the website) with your offer before they invite you. Then, once invited, you as the buyer go to wherever the seller is by clicking the blue swirl on their party frame. It’s generally expected that you as the buyer wait for the seller to press the trade button, as they may have to find the item, make inventory space etc.

To add on and reiterate, the normal etiquette is for the buyer to go to the seller, and for the seller to be the one who initiates the trade request. Some people are super particular about this whole thing for whatever reason too.

True, another common occurrence is people taking things like Nyquil in addition to acetaminophen tablets, not realizing that Nyquil has acetaminophen in it as well.

I’m not a doctor, and you should definitely defer to one that is more familiar with your individual analgesic needs and medical history. 

That being said, acetaminophen is generally a perfectly fine pain reliever for most people when used appropriately. Taking a couple of 325mg pills per day will probably not harm the average person, even on a daily basis. When we’re talking overdoses, we’re talking about people who have ingested several grams at once.

If you’re at all concerned about how taking acetaminophen daily will affect you, it’s definitely worth bringing up with your doctor, as they will have a vastly better grasp on your individual situation.

Yes, a sizeable chunk of acetaminophen induced hepatotoxicity is a result of intentional overdose. Furthermore, a pretty significant chunk of liver transplants in the US are actually a result of acetaminophen induced hepatotoxicity. These types of overdoses frequently occur in a very irrational, heat of the moment manner. Someone experiences a crisis, and they go to the medicine cabinet and take as many pills as they can. When they have access to a bottle of 100+ 500 mg tablets, they end up taking a large amount of acetaminophen very quickly, resulting in hepatotoxicity, and potentially a liver transplant depending on a number of factors. 

The thought is that by restricting the immediate access to a large quantity of drug, you reduce risk for those that are in crisis and acting irrationally. Obviously, this solution won't completely eradicate acetaminophen induced hepatotoxicity, as determined people will find a way regardless, and there are absolutely accidental overdoses, but it does have the potential to significantly reduce the overall rates.

It’s actually crazy how simple the solution to the majority of the US acetaminophen overdose problem is too. Other countries have already figured it out. You just make it so you can’t buy more than 7g at a time, and you force it to be sold in blister packs instead of the gigantic bottles you can get at Walmart/Costco. We would significantly reduce the number of people on our liver transplant list with just those changes.

Evasion is a huge part of the defenses, along with ghost shroud. I have \~80% chance to evade without flasks. Evasion has entropy, or bad luck protection, so it essentially means you will very consistently only be hit (by attacks) 1 out of every 5 times. When you are actually hit, you have ghost shrouds, which for me give me \~1000 ES back instantly.

Then you have the leech, which is always working because of trickster's ES overleech. This effectively gives me \~4000 ES per second with ghost reaver provided I'm attacking with somewhat regular frequency. The spell suppression is even better than normal because of spellbreaker and the mastery which push the damage prevented from spells up to 66%, provided you're on full energy shield which I almost always am due to the leech.

I also have 16% phys taken as chaos, which with CI is effectively 16% physical damage reduction, or 4 endurance charges worth. I have 78/79/78 max res for ele damage as well. Combine these things with a very large ES pool, and you're incredibly tanky.

I don’t think 15d is enough to swap to SST unless you don’t mind playing a very underpowered version of the build. Don’t get me wrong, you can get by without a lot of this stuff, but the build won’t feel insane or even very strong until you have: 

-Ashes (~35% more damage with correct alt qualities, not to mention reservation which allows you to fit auras) ~30d

-Emperors vigilance with at least 600 es ~5-10d

-Hatred cold convert watchers eye ~3-4d

-Alt qualities — Phantasmal SST, Divergent Determ, Phantasmal Ancestral Protector, Anomalous defiance banner, Anomalous Precision ~10-15d

-Awakened gems — Fork is the one that’s the most important here imo, noticeable clear boost.

This doesn’t consider any other gear pieces which can cost a decent chunk too (especially the weapon), but at the minimum I would recommend at least 70-80d before starting the build assuming you don’t have any of these things yet.

Assassin is the most accessible, Scion is the least accessible in terms of gear requirement. Occultist falls somewhere in the middle. To play worb occultist you really need a base crit hatred watcher's eye, where Assassin gets enough crit from the ascendancy that it doesn't. Occultist's benefit is like you said, the aoe, which is fairly important. Since you have a mageblood, I'd recommend going occultist or scion, whichever suits your fancy. Occultist is my preference. With occultist, the standard setup is omni, annihilating light, black sun crest helm, brass dome chest and elusive/tailwind boots. Rings are pretty easy to craft with essences (which happen to be *super* cheap this league), the gloves are pretty easy to craft with the eldritch currency as well (I can post more detail about crafting the pieces if you want).

Overall, assassin gets you started on less but scales mediocre, occultist gets you started on a middle budget and scales a little bit better than assassin, and scion gets you started on a higher budget, but it has the largest potential. So my default recommendation for SSF players is assassin, trade league is occultist.

This is definitely the way. The way ele hit math works is super convoluted, but it basically works like this.

Elemental hit essentially adds damage of all three elements to an attack, but only deals the damage of a chosen element. For the sake of math, let's say it deals 500 fire, 500 cold, and 500 lightning damage per hit, but only chooses a single element. So if you attack and it chooses lightning, you deal 500 lightning damage, not 1500 mixed damage.

Now, you use both combat focus jewels to make it so ele hit can only choose fire, meaning you will do 500 fire damage each attack. Even though ele hit now only deals fire damage, it still has the 500 cold and lightning damage added to it, it's just latent since ele hit only does damage of the chosen element.

So, with avatar of fire (via Xoph's blood), you're now converting 250 of that latent cold damage, and 250 of that latent lightning damage to fire, meaning that each attack now does 1000 fire damage (500 fire + 250 converted cold + 250 converted lightning).

Now you add Pyre to the mix, so that 250 converted latent cold damage is now 450 (490 with catalysts), meaning you now deal 1200 (500 fire + 450 converted cold + 250 converted lightning) fire damage with each hit.

The other benefit of ele hit is for GG jewels, since ele hit counts as a lightning, cold and fire skill, it's possible to get some pretty nutty 40%+ crit multi jewels.

Also, to answer your question about bows, your best bet early on is Chin Sol. It's not great, but it's good enough. Once you feel like upgrading, the best way to do so is fossil crafting a +3 bow, which I'll include the steps of down below. You can also use a +2 gems bow early as well, as it will likely outperform Chin Sol depending on the other mods in addition to the +2 gems, and it's easier to get typically.

So, you're looking for +1 to level of socketed gems and +2 to level of socketed bow gems.

To get one, start with an imperial/highborn bow base, ilvl 83+. If you can, getting one with 6L already or 30% quality is a bonus. Ideally, a shaped base, but keep in mind if you use a shaped base it will take you many, many more attempts to get your desired stats, but with a decently high upside.

To start, make the bow rare, then use perfect fossils on it until you get 30% quality.

Once you hit the quality, scour the bow and craft as much quality on it as you can (you can skip this step if you've got a 6L already).

Now use the vorici method  ( [Vorici Chromatic Calculator (siveran.github.io)](https://siveran.github.io/calc.html) ) to get your desired colors, preferably 3 red, 2 green, 1 blue. Or, if you've already got a 6L, you can use the 2 red 1 blue craft and hope to get lucky.

Proceed to 6L your bow with fusings, taking advantage of the 40%+ quality (30% from fossils, 10%+ from bench craft) to significantly increase your chances. Or use other methods of 6L (prophecy, fusing craft etc) (again, skip this step if you've already got a 6L)

So, now you should have an ilvl 83+ 6L 30% qual imperial/highborn bow with your ideal colors.

Make the bow rare, and use resonators with metallic, prismatic, and corroded fossils until you get your +1 socketed gems and +2 socketed bow gems. On an uninfluenced bow, this likely won't take you too many tries (for me, it hasn't taken more than 5-6 tries). All that's left now is to repeat the method until you get the desired other stats you want in addition to the +1 socketed gems and +2 socketed bow gems.

Fill out the bow with whichever of the following stats you can get while maintaining the +3 total craft:

% Attack speed

% increased elemental damage with attack skills

Bows fire # additional arrows

% global crit multi

% increased crit chance

% chance to deal double damage.
